body: You have to type cast `$value` to string when calling `__()`. Given that the default value of second argument of `__()` is null there's no way to differentiate between no argument passed versus argument with null value.
Well, there would be a way to determine that, right? The func_get_args() count.
Another way is using array for second argument.
Yes, both might be applicable as BC way. We should investigate that IMO.
I think that also, if {0} is part of $text, it should at least not be returned if func_get_args count > 0

When 2 arguments are passed the 2nd already gets [typecast to array](https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/master/src/I18n/functions.php#L32), so the problem isn't with `__()` function but it seems translators don't handle `null`.
Can we foreach cast all `null` internally here to fix this bug as a quickfix?

issue.title: Handle explict null values in translation functions

issue.body:
When we get an explicit null we should use that as a translation value that is interpolated into the message. This had to be done in 3.4 as we have access to `...` which makes this change simpler to implement.

Refs #10087
